newsitem.title: UK: Philippines sets Brady exchange rate at 2.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sets Brady exchange rate at 2.25 pct.

text.p: The Republic of the Philippines on Monday fixed the terms of its Brady exchange offer at 2.25 percent over US Treasuries for the 20-year fixed rate issue.

In a statement released in London the Philippines said the clearing above the UST benchmark rate for the fixed rate bonds was 2.25 percent, the yield was 9.25 percent and the fixed rate semi-annual coupon was 8.75 percent.
JP Morgan is arranging the exchange.

Under the terms of the exchange, dated September 2, 1996, the Philippines is exchanging U.S. dollar-denominated series B principal collateralised interest reduction bonds, due in 2017, and dollar-denominated series A principal collateralised interest reduction bonds due in 2018, for new dollar-denominated fixed-rate bonds due in 2016.
The Philippines said that because the offers to exchange the 2017 and 2018 bonds for floating rate bonds would result in issuance of less than $200 million, no floating rate bonds will be issued.

However, people who submitted non-competitive offers to exchange the 2017 and 2018 issus for floating rate bonds will have the option to exchange them for fixed rate bonds at the applicable exchange value, the statement said.
The issue price of the fixed rate bond is 0.95481.

The maximum aggregate principal amount of fixed rate bonds to be issued is $690 million. The maximum aggregate principal amount of 2017 bonds to be exchanged is $628.093 million, while the maximum amount of 2018 bonds is $6.552 million.
Settlement date is 7 October 1996, and trading in the fixed rate bonds will start today.
For the 2017 bonds, the exchange value per $1,000 principal amount is $867.64, while the exchange value for the 2018 bonds is $866.33, the statement said.
Invitations for offers expired on 20 September 1996. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
